Hood Heroes - épisode 11 : Lex Garcia, e: Hood Heroes - Episode 11: Lex Garcia and Writing as a Lifeline
« À la base, je suis écrivain. Mais je s: “At heart, I’m a writer. But I’m also a chiller!”

“At heart, I’m a writer. But I’m also a chiller!” That humorous line kicks off our conversation with Lex Garcia. Born Alexander de Gracia, the Montréal millennial is now a screenwriter and one of the new faces of television writing. Of Panamanian descent, Lex tells La Converse about a path marked by unique experiences and about his sense of belonging to the east end of the city.
À travers son récit, Lex a un message d’: Through his story, Lex has a message of hope for young people in the city’s neighbourhoods.
Avec un énorme sourire et un peu de timi: With a huge smile and a bit of shyness at first, Lex settles into the La Converse studios. “When people ask me who I am and how I would describe myself, what always comes up is that I’m from Panama and I come from the East,” Lex begins, smiling. Calling himself a “lover of the street,” the Canadian-Panamanian says he has “hung around pretty much everywhere with everybody.” “Me gusta la calle (I like the street, Ed.), I like going out, I like parties, I like events, and so on,” he lists.
Comme n’importe qui, Lex estime avoir un: Like anyone, Lex considers his path fairly ordinary. “I moved a lot, I went to several schools. I figured out quickly how the academic system works here: I knew what to do to stay out of trouble, I knew what to say so my teachers would leave me alone,” he says.
Il y a quelques années, alors qu’il enta: A few years ago, while he was starting a psychology degree, Lex found himself questioning things. Writing had always been there, on the side, but he didn’t know how to make it part of his identity. So, after a series of chance events, he ended up “making the right jokes at the right time in front of the right people.” He recalls his reaction when VICE Media took one of his projects into consideration: “I was waiting for the bus in the Rivière (Rivière-des-Prairies, Ed.), and I got a call from an unknown number. My first reflex: don’t answer, block the number. Guys from the hood, we panic,” he says, laughing. “Then the same number called right back. When I answered, I found out it was a guy who worked for VICE and he was interested in one of my pitches,” he recounts, with stars in his eyes, as if reliving the moment.
« Je n’ai pas d’attachement particulier: “I don’t have a special attachment to any one neighbourhood, but I have to admit I have a lot of affection for Villeray. Villeray is the Mecca of Latinos in Montréal,” he begins, speaking of his attachment to his culture of origin. “The Panamanian community in Montréal is very small. We all know each other, and we recognize each other by our accent when we speak Spanish with other Spanish speakers.”
À Villeray, il y a une importante commun: Villeray has a large Latin American community. Lex talks about it a lot when explaining his sense of belonging to Latin American culture. “I learned to dance salsa and bachata* at Salvadorans’ places; I spent so much time at Colombian parties and I ate the best food from the Peruvian community! By the way, shout out to Peruvian food. Best food in the world!” he takes the time to say. For Lex, it’s these contributions that, one by one, build Latin American culture in Montréal.
Il se rappelle d’ailleurs le temps où il: He also remembers the time when he hung out in the streets of the East End of the island. “The best Latino shops are in Villeray,” he maintains. “My parents would go rent movie cassettes at a market that sold them under the table in Spanish, and that’s kind of how I didn’t lose my mother tongue,” he says in a childlike tone.
Si son parcours est parsemé de petites p: Although his path is dotted with small adventures, the writer remains aware that success is hard to come by – in every field, of course, but especially in those we’re passionate about and that seem impossible to reach.
« Qui dit travail, dit effort ; et qui d: “Work means effort, and effort means failure, eventually”: that is how the screenwriter describes his view of the world. He continues: “I started in music. I was very motivated, I worked hard. Today, I admit, I wasn’t very good,” he confides after a shy laugh.
Être perdu fait partie du processus, exp: Being lost is part of the process, he explains. “There’s struggle – la lucha, in Spanish – in everything. But what matters is to keep going. Where there’s a failure, there’s also a chance to reinvent yourself,” he says, determined.
Sur une note un peu plus personnelle, il: On a slightly more personal note, he admits: “I hate writing, but I hate not writing even more.” Lex has been writing since he was 13. During harder times in his life and adolescence, writing helped him fight his problems. “In my writing, I often talk about dramedy. The best drama is always funny, he says. That’s kind of the spirit of life. There are some moments that are more complicated than others. But what matters is to learn from those episodes. That’s the spirit of art too.”
Ce qui est aussi important pour Lex, c’e: What is also important to Lex is showing resilience and flexibility. “Nothing in life is an L (a loss, Ed.) or a fumble (a missed opportunity, Ed.). From that failure, how can I succeed? That’s the question you have to ask yourself in hard times,” he says.
<strong>Il faut une communauté pour élev: It takes a community to raise a young person
Au sujet des difficultés auxquelles les: On the difficulties teenagers in Montréal’s neighbourhoods face, Lex Garcia reiterates the importance of community and its great benefits in a young person’s life.
« Ce que ça prend, c’est une communauté: “What it takes is a community to raise a young person. It’s an ability not to isolate yourself, and that starts with us. It doesn’t even start with the child in question,” he begins calmly.
« Ce qui forme la vie d’un enfant, ce n’: “What shapes a child’s life isn’t only their family or loved ones. It’s everything they see, everything around them. It’s the guy at the convenience store who makes sure they’re not foxing (skipping class, Ed.). It’s also the older people in the neighbourhood who have to keep an eye on them and the other younger ones,” he lists.
Il y a aussi le concept de « responsabil: The Hood Hero also raises the concept of “community accountability.” “Young people need to feel safe and comfortable at home, close to their landmarks. Violence takes different forms. A child who commits offences is not a criminal. Defining a person by the sum of their misdeeds makes them one-dimensional. But a person has many facets – and it’s even more complex with young people.”
« Lorsqu’on voit des jeunes qui ont des: “When we see young people who have a bout (firearm, Ed.) on them or who zak (steal, Ed.) cars, for example, we need to ask ourselves a question: where are we falling short as a community? We have to keep in mind that some people’s actions reflect other people’s shortcomings. That’s where the conversation with youth is,” he says.
Lex estime que ces lacunes communautaire: Lex believes these community shortcomings show up very early in a young person’s support system. “At school, if you’re not good academically or at sports, nothing will be offered to you. It’s wack (disappointing, Ed.). I was lucky: I started working at 12; I kept myself busy early.”
Il y a également un énorme problème d’ab: There is also a huge problem of abandonment of young people who are – or who become – struggling. “We don’t keep all young people busy. We only keep busy those who can be productive, those who do arts or sports. We leave the others behind. But we have to take care of all young people, no matter what they like or don’t like.”
Lex écrit d’ailleurs beaucoup sur l’isol: Lex also writes a lot about isolation. “The individual is a link in the community. When they’re weak, the whole community is doing poorly. I think we have to take care of those who isolate themselves, and it’s even more important and necessary to do so with young people. Teenagers who isolate themselves are still developing. Their brains are still growing, and the decisions they make matter for their development. We have to take care of our youth,” explains the former psychology student.
Sa manière de soutenir sa communauté, c’: His way of supporting his community is to write about it. “Nobody asked me to write about them. But my way of giving is to devote my time to this reality and to reflect what I see in my art,” he explains. It’s also about becoming a positive example for younger people, for those around him or who see him from afar. Lex believes that helping those who helped him “is also giving back.”
« J’écris pour tout le monde. Mais j’ent: “I write for everyone. But I start a dialogue with my community first and foremost. Maybe I don’t always succeed, but at least I try,” concludes Lex Garcia.
